title: Diagonal nerve detects weak equivalences between cofibrant homotopy groupoids
statement: Fix a small set $O$. Use the fixed-object model structure on simplicial categories on $O$ and functors fixing $O$ from [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], for the $O\times O$-sorted algebraic theory of associative composition and identities. Weak equivalences and fibrations are weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations on each mapping simplicial set. Cofibrant means that the map from the identity-only category on $O$ has the left lifting property against every mappingwise trivial Kan fibration. Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $u:U\to V$ be an object-preserving simplicial functor between cofibrant objects in this model structure. Suppose that both ordinary path-component categories $\pi_0U$ and $\pi_0V$ are groupoids; their morphisms are path components of the mapping simplicial sets. For a simplicial category $T$ on $O$, put $B(T)_{p,q}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p\in O}\prod_{r=1}^p T(x_{r-1},x_r)_q$; the first-direction operators compose or omit arrows and insert identities, and the second-direction operators are those of the mapping sets. Empty products are singletons. Its diagonal classifying nerve is $NT=\operatorname{diag}B(T)$. Then $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set if and only if $Nu:NU\to NV$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets. No Kan, connectedness, or nonemptiness assumption is imposed on the mapping sets or on $O$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Corollary 9.6, printed p.280; the diagonal nerve is 1.4(vi), and the fixed-object model is 7.2. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy theorem.
